info.title: Belgian Constitutional Court Rulings Search API
info.description: Hosted, read-only search API over Belgian Constitutional Court rulings (Dutch-language, POC scope). Returns ranked, cited passages from official rulings using hybrid BM25 + vector retrieval. This API is designed to be called by an AI agent or assistant (Microsoft Copilot Studio declarative agent, ChatGPT Custom GPT Action, or MCP server) on behalf of a non-technical end user who asked a plain-language question about Constitutional Court case law. The API does not synthesize answers itself - it only retrieves and returns cited source passages; the calling LLM is responsible for composing the final answer and MUST include the citation fields (ecli, case_number, ruling_date) for every ruling it references, plus a link to source_pdf_url so a human can verify the passage against the original PDF.

servers.description: REPLACE ME: Scaleway Serverless Container endpoint for the query service. This is a placeholder - after running `terraform apply`, copy the real container URL from the Terraform output (e.g. `terraform output query_service_url`) and replace this value before importing this spec into Copilot Studio / the Custom GPT Action builder. The URL is region-scoped to Scaleway fr-par (Paris) per the project's EU-data-residency requirement.

tags.name: search
tags.description: Retrieval endpoints over the indexed corpus of Constitutional Court rulings.

tags.name: infrastructure
tags.description: Operational endpoints for deployment/monitoring, not intended for the AI agent to call on a user's behalf.

get.description: Runs a hybrid BM25 (lexical) + vector (semantic) search over the indexed corpus of Belgian Constitutional Court rulings and returns the top-ranked matching passages, each tagged with full case metadata for citation. Call this action whenever a user asks a question about Belgian Constitutional Court case law - for example a conceptual/topical question (e.g. 'What has the Court decided about environmental permits?'), or an exact-lookup question naming a specific citation, case number, docket number, or article. Every result includes everything needed to cite the source correctly: at minimum, always cite the `ecli`, `case_number`, and `ruling_date` together in the answer, and include a link to `source_pdf_url` so the user can open and verify the original official PDF. Do not present retrieved passages as legal advice - they are excerpts of official rulings for the calling assistant to summarize and cite, not a substitute for the source text.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: The search query. Accepts either a natural-language question in Dutch or English (e.g. 'Wat besliste het Grondwettelijk Hof over energiepremies?' or 'rulings about environmental permits in 2024') or an exact citation to look up directly (e.g. an ECLI such as 'ECLI:BE:GHCC:2025:ARR.001', an case number such as '1/2025', a role/docket number such as '8115', or a file slug such as '2025-001n'). Do not rephrase or truncate a citation the user typed - pass it through as-is so exact-match lexical search can find it.

schema.example: Wat besliste het Hof over de vernietiging van een fiscale norm in 2024?

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of ranked passages to return. Keep this small (the default) for a normal chat answer; only raise it if the user explicitly asks for a broader survey of rulings on a topic.

200.description: Ranked search results. May be an empty `results` array if nothing in the Dutch-language corpus matches the query closely enough - in that case, tell the user no relevant ruling was found rather than guessing.

401.description: Missing or invalid `X-API-Key` header. This indicates a connector/action configuration problem (the shared key), not a user-facing issue - end users never supply this key themselves.

422.description: The `q` parameter was missing or empty, or `limit` was out of range.

get.description: Lightweight liveness/readiness check for the query service (e.g. for Scaleway container health probes or manual verification after deployment). It does not require the shared API key and does not touch the indexed case data. This endpoint is not intended to be called by the AI agent as part of answering a user's question - it exists for the maintainer and infrastructure tooling only.

200.description: The service is up and able to serve requests.

ApiKeyAuth.name: X-API-Key
ApiKeyAuth.description: Shared static API key for the query service, issued once by the maintainer. It is configured as a fixed value on the connector/action itself (Copilot Studio custom connector credentials, or the Custom GPT Action's API key auth) and is never seen or entered by the end user chatting with the agent. See docs/copilot-studio-setup.md and docs/custom-gpt-setup.md for exactly where to set this during setup.

query.description: The `q` value that was actually searched, echoed back for traceability.

results.description: Ranked passages matching the query, best match first. May be empty if no ruling matched closely enough.

SearchResultItem.description: One ranked passage from a single Constitutional Court ruling, together with the full metadata needed to cite it correctly. ecli, case_number, docket_number, and case_number are distinct identifiers from the source documents and must not be conflated or substituted for one another when citing a ruling.

ecli.description: Canonical citation identifier for the ruling (European Case Law Identifier), e.g. 'ECLI:BE:GHCC:2025:ARR.001'. Always include this verbatim when citing the ruling in an answer.

case_number.description: Official arrest (judgment) number as published by the Court, e.g. '1/2025'. Always include this alongside the ECLI and ruling date when citing.

docket_number.description: Role/docket number ('rolnummer') of the underlying case before the Court, e.g. '8115'. Distinct from the case number and case number - do not use interchangeably.

case_number.description: File/URL slug used by the Court's own website for this ruling, e.g. '2025-001n'. Distinct from the ECLI, case number, and docket number.

ruling_date.description: Date the ruling was rendered (ISO 8601, YYYY-MM-DD). Always include this alongside the ECLI and case number when citing.

language.description: ISO 639-1 language code of the ruling text. The POC corpus is Dutch-only, so this is currently always 'nl'.

procedure_type.description: The type of procedure before the Court, e.g. 'Prejudiciële vraag' (preliminary question) or 'Beroep tot vernietiging' (annulment action).

controlled_norm.description: The law or article that was under constitutional review in this ruling.

outcome.description: The Court's ruling outcome, e.g. 'Vernietiging' (annulment), 'Verwerping' (rejection), or 'Handhaving van de gevolgen' (maintenance of effects).

title.description: Short human-readable title for the ruling, suitable for display in a chat answer.

section.description: Which structural section of the ruling this passage comes from: 'facts', 'arguments' (the parties' '-A-' submissions), 'reasoning' (the Court's '-B-' analysis), or 'ruling' (the operative decision).

excerpt.description: The matched passage text itself, in Dutch. Quote or closely paraphrase this in the answer rather than inventing wording.

source_pdf_url.description: URL of the original official PDF on the Court's website (https://nl.const-court.be/). Always surface this as a link in the answer so the user can verify the passage against the source document.

score.description: Hybrid BM25 + vector reciprocal-rank-fusion relevance score. Higher is more relevant. Useful for ordering or filtering results, not meaningful as an absolute probability.

status.description: Liveness indicator for the query service.

ErrorResponse.description: Generic error body returned for authentication and validation failures.
